# Consumer catalog pilots

Run `bash kits/catalog-kit/pilots/run.sh` from the agentic-kit checkout. The platform checkout (set `KIT_PLATFORM_DIR`, plus `KIT_PLATFORM_REVIEW_PATH`, `KIT_PLATFORM_ENV_PATH` and `KIT_PLATFORM_REVIEW_MODULE`; any unset means the run skips) must contain commit `821c509035a8bbd98907c83b54372bec70116425` locally. Its current HEAD may be advanced or dirty. The script refuses an unavailable pin and archives that exact commit under `TMPDIR` or `/tmp` (override the parent with an existing external `PILOT_SCRATCH_ROOT`). It refuses scratch space inside either the kit or consumer checkout, including symlink aliases, before creating any snapshot. It injects the two `.go.txt` test templates into the snapshot and runs race tests. It never writes to the consumer checkout. The snapshot and `go.work` remain for inspection. `CONSUMER_REVISION` accepts another full 40-character commit SHA for runner testing; a custom revision is not the recorded consumer replay. Run `go test -race ./kits/catalog-kit/pilots` for hermetic disposable-Git runner regressions.

Review Kit: project two CUE-loaded `FlattenCatalogs` layers through catalog-kit's explicit dependency DAG. The second layer is authored into the archived replay and adds `pilot.added`. Compare common order and per-key provenance against `BuildStandard`, and retain authored typed definitions, source line spans, content hashes and origins in sidecars. `BuildStandard` also computes the effective exception-policy intersection; that domain-owned value stays outside common metadata. Consumer semantic-floor tests cover weakening refusal. The common catalog is only a metadata projection; the consumer remains the typed authority.

Env Kit: project baseline and changed extension metadata as dependent layers, compare every effective key and typed entry against sidecars, prove a declared addition and a refinement survive, and require a contradictory row to return `ExtensionConflictError`. The CUE loader remains the authority. Both projections encode UTF-8 stable keys injectively in path slugs and test that inserting a sibling leaves existing IDs intact.

These tests prove bounded offline integration against this exact revision. They do not migrate either consumer or establish production adoption or measured savings. Existing module-cache dependencies are used; the script does not invoke a provider or service.
